re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1232: [REFACTOR] CLI/app god-files at/over the 2800-line ceiling are the merge-conflict magnets — split bin/fah.dart, agent_cli.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_service.dart

## Description

**Data over the last 40 merged PRs** (2026-10-03/04, 369 file-touches): the highest-churn files are simultaneously the biggest files — classic god-file conflict physics:

| file | PRs touching it | current lines | vs 2800 guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart | **11 (27.5%)** | 2737 | 63 under |
| bin/fah.dart | 6 | **2826** | **OVER** |
| .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml | 6 | — | — |
| lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart (barrel) | 5 | 260 | — |
| lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart + agent_cli_config.dart | 5+5 | 1541/783 | — |
| lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart | 4 | **2799** | **1 under** |
| flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart | 4 | **2815** | **OVER** |

Every fourth PR fights over agent_cli.dart; every long-lived PR (30–65h lead: #1143 65h, #1163 55h, #1165 55h, #1161/#1166/#1173 49h) must rebase across the serial main queue through these same files. Size and churn compound: the bigger the file, the higher the probability two PRs edit adjacent regions.

**Also suspicious**: bin/fah.dart (2826) and agent_service.dart (2815) are OVER the pre-commit 2800-line guard yet keep landing — verify the guard actually covers them (exempt-list hole?).

**Proposed cuts:**
1. **bin/fah.dart → bin/thin + lib/src/cli/fah_commands/**: one file per subcommand family (trajectory/session/bench/…), main keeps arg routing only.
2. **agent_cli.dart**: it is already a part-of library (approval_commands etc.) — finish the pattern: slash-command tables self-register from part files so the main file stops being the edit magnet for every new command.
3. **agent_service.dart** split by concern: session lifecycle / provider wiring / secrets / mail fabric.
4. **builtin_tools.dart**: per-tool-family assembly files under lib/src/tools/.
5. **Barrel policy** (flutter_agent_harness.dart, 5/40 touches): grouped append-only export sections with a one-line convention comment, or per-subsystem mini-barrels — pick one, write it in AGENTS.md.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: bin/fah.dart, agent_service.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_cli.dart each < 2000 lines after the split; zero behavior change (existing test suites green, no public API moves without deprecation).
- AC2: the pre-commit size guard demonstrably fires on a file > 2800 in bin/ and flutter_app/ (test: temporary oversized file → hook rejects).
- AC3: re-measure after the next 40 merged PRs: agent_cli.dart touch rate < 15%, no file above 2400 lines in the top-10 churn list.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1232 AC2 — size-guard self-test                                        ║
# ║  Proves the 2800-line guard fires on oversized files in bin/ and           ║
# ║  flutter_app/lib/ through BOTH paths a file can reach main:                ║
# ║    A. CI whole-tree scan   (ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size)     ║
# ║    B. pre-commit staged scan (ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size)        ║
# ║  Method: drop two temporary 2801-line .dart files (one per directory),     ║
# ║  expect rejection, then remove them and expect the guard to pass again     ║
# ║  (negative control). The temp files never reach a commit; the index is     ║
# ║  restored exactly (only the two temp paths are ever staged/reset).         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh
# Exit 0 = guard demonstrably fires on both paths; non-zero = hole remains.

set -euo pipefail

TMP_BIN="bin/fah_size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
TMP_APP="flutter_app/lib/size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
OVER=2801   # MAX_LINES (2800) + 1

cleanup() {
  git reset -q -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

make_oversized() {
  # 2801 comment lines — syntactically valid Dart, over the ceiling.
  { echo "// size-guard probe (gh-1232 AC2 self-test) — DO NOT COMMIT"
    i=1
    while [ "$i" -lt "$OVER" ]; do echo '// padding'; i=$((i + 1)); done
  } > "$1"
}

expect_reject() {
  # $1 = label, $2.. = command to run (already staged temps assumed)
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  set +e
  out=$("$@" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): guard PASSED an oversized file" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "FILE SIZE"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejected, but not by the size guard:" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejection did not name the probe file" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "✅ $label: guard rejected the oversized files"
}

echo "✅ pre-flight: hook size stage passes without probes"

make_oversized "$TMP_APP"

echo "── A. CI whole-tree scan ──"

echo "║  ✅ AC2 SELF-TEST PASSED — the 2800-line guard fires on bin/ and           ║"

# gh-1232: [REFACTOR] CLI/app god-files at/over the 2800-line ceiling are the merge-conflict magnets — split bin/fah.dart, agent_cli.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_service.dart

## Description

**Data over the last 40 merged PRs** (2026-10-03/04, 369 file-touches): the highest-churn files are simultaneously the biggest files — classic god-file conflict physics:

| file | PRs touching it | current lines | vs 2800 guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart | **11 (27.5%)** | 2737 | 63 under |
| bin/fah.dart | 6 | **2826** | **OVER** |
| .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml | 6 | — | — |
| lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart (barrel) | 5 | 260 | — |
| lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart + agent_cli_config.dart | 5+5 | 1541/783 | — |
| lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart | 4 | **2799** | **1 under** |
| flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart | 4 | **2815** | **OVER** |

Every fourth PR fights over agent_cli.dart; every long-lived PR (30–65h lead: #1143 65h, #1163 55h, #1165 55h, #1161/#1166/#1173 49h) must rebase across the serial main queue through these same files. Size and churn compound: the bigger the file, the higher the probability two PRs edit adjacent regions.

**Also suspicious**: bin/fah.dart (2826) and agent_service.dart (2815) are OVER the pre-commit 2800-line guard yet keep landing — verify the guard actually covers them (exempt-list hole?).

**Proposed cuts:**
1. **bin/fah.dart → bin/thin + lib/src/cli/fah_commands/**: one file per subcommand family (trajectory/session/bench/…), main keeps arg routing only.
2. **agent_cli.dart**: it is already a part-of library (approval_commands etc.) — finish the pattern: slash-command tables self-register from part files so the main file stops being the edit magnet for every new command.
3. **agent_service.dart** split by concern: session lifecycle / provider wiring / secrets / mail fabric.
4. **builtin_tools.dart**: per-tool-family assembly files under lib/src/tools/.
5. **Barrel policy** (flutter_agent_harness.dart, 5/40 touches): grouped append-only export sections with a one-line convention comment, or per-subsystem mini-barrels — pick one, write it in AGENTS.md.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: bin/fah.dart, agent_service.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_cli.dart each < 2000 lines after the split; zero behavior change (existing test suites green, no public API moves without deprecation).
- AC2: the pre-commit size guard demonstrably fires on a file > 2800 in bin/ and flutter_app/ (test: temporary oversized file → hook rejects).
- AC3: re-measure after the next 40 merged PRs: agent_cli.dart touch rate < 15%, no file above 2400 lines in the top-10 churn list.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1232 AC2 — size-guard self-test                                        ║
# ║  Proves the 2800-line guard fires on oversized files in bin/ and           ║
# ║  flutter_app/lib/ through BOTH paths a file can reach main:                ║
# ║    A. CI whole-tree scan   (ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size)     ║
# ║    B. pre-commit staged scan (ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size)        ║
# ║  Method: drop two temporary 2801-line .dart files (one per directory),     ║
# ║  expect rejection, then remove them and expect the guard to pass again     ║
# ║  (negative control). The temp files never reach a commit; the index is     ║
# ║  restored exactly (only the two temp paths are ever staged/reset).         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh
# Exit 0 = guard demonstrably fires on both paths; non-zero = hole remains.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

TMP_BIN="bin/fah_size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
TMP_APP="flutter_app/lib/size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
OVER=2801   # MAX_LINES (2800) + 1

cleanup() {
  git reset -q -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

make_oversized() {
  # 2801 comment lines — syntactically valid Dart, over the ceiling.
  { echo "// size-guard probe (gh-1232 AC2 self-test) — DO NOT COMMIT"
    i=1
    while [ "$i" -lt "$OVER" ]; do echo '// padding'; i=$((i + 1)); done
  } > "$1"
}

expect_reject() {
  # $1 = label, $2.. = command to run (already staged temps assumed)
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  set +e
  out=$("$@" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): guard PASSED an oversized file" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "FILE SIZE"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejected, but not by the size guard:" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejection did not name the probe file" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "✅ $label: guard rejected the oversized files"
}

echo "── gh-1232 AC2 size-guard self-test ──"

# Pre-flight: the negative control must pass with NO probe files staged.
out=$(bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size 2>&1) \
  || { echo "❌ pre-flight: hook size stage fails on a clean tree:" >&2; echo "$out" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "✅ pre-flight: hook size stage passes without probes"

make_oversized "$TMP_BIN"
make_oversized "$TMP_APP"

echo "── A. CI whole-tree scan ──"
expect_reject "CI scan (bin/ + flutter_app/lib/)" \
  bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size

echo "── B. pre-commit staged scan ──"
git add -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
expect_reject "hook staged scan (bin/ + flutter_app/lib/)" \
  bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size

echo "── negative control: probes removed, guard passes again ──"
cleanup
trap - EXIT
out=$(bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size 2>&1) \
  || { echo "❌ negative control: guard still fails after probe cleanup:" >&2; echo "$out" >&2; exit 1; }
[ ! -e "$TMP_BIN" ] && [ ! -e "$TMP_APP" ] \
  || { echo "❌ probe files left behind" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "✅ negative control: guard passes, probes gone"

echo ""
echo "╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
echo "║  ✅ AC2 SELF-TEST PASSED — the 2800-line guard fires on bin/ and           ║"
echo "║     flutter_app/ through both the CI scan and the pre-commit staged scan   ║"
echo "╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"

# gh-1232: [REFACTOR] CLI/app god-files at/over the 2800-line ceiling are the merge-conflict magnets — split bin/fah.dart, agent_cli.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_service.dart

## Description

**Data over the last 40 merged PRs** (2026-10-03/04, 369 file-touches): the highest-churn files are simultaneously the biggest files — classic god-file conflict physics:

| file | PRs touching it | current lines | vs 2800 guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart | **11 (27.5%)** | 2737 | 63 under |
| bin/fah.dart | 6 | **2826** | **OVER** |
| .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml | 6 | — | — |
| lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart (barrel) | 5 | 260 | — |
| lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart + agent_cli_config.dart | 5+5 | 1541/783 | — |
| lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart | 4 | **2799** | **1 under** |
| flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart | 4 | **2815** | **OVER** |

Every fourth PR fights over agent_cli.dart; every long-lived PR (30–65h lead: #1143 65h, #1163 55h, #1165 55h, #1161/#1166/#1173 49h) must rebase across the serial main queue through these same files. Size and churn compound: the bigger the file, the higher the probability two PRs edit adjacent regions.

**Also suspicious**: bin/fah.dart (2826) and agent_service.dart (2815) are OVER the pre-commit 2800-line guard yet keep landing — verify the guard actually covers them (exempt-list hole?).

**Proposed cuts:**
1. **bin/fah.dart → bin/thin + lib/src/cli/fah_commands/**: one file per subcommand family (trajectory/session/bench/…), main keeps arg routing only.
2. **agent_cli.dart**: it is already a part-of library (approval_commands etc.) — finish the pattern: slash-command tables self-register from part files so the main file stops being the edit magnet for every new command.
3. **agent_service.dart** split by concern: session lifecycle / provider wiring / secrets / mail fabric.
4. **builtin_tools.dart**: per-tool-family assembly files under lib/src/tools/.
5. **Barrel policy** (flutter_agent_harness.dart, 5/40 touches): grouped append-only export sections with a one-line convention comment, or per-subsystem mini-barrels — pick one, write it in AGENTS.md.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: bin/fah.dart, agent_service.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_cli.dart each < 2000 lines after the split; zero behavior change (existing test suites green, no public API moves without deprecation).
- AC2: the pre-commit size guard demonstrably fires on a file > 2800 in bin/ and flutter_app/ (test: temporary oversized file → hook rejects).
- AC3: re-measure after the next 40 merged PRs: agent_cli.dart touch rate < 15%, no file above 2400 lines in the top-10 churn list.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

# ║  gh-1232 AC2 — size-guard self-test                                        ║
# ║  Proves the 2800-line guard fires on oversized files in bin/ and           ║
# ║  flutter_app/lib/ through BOTH paths a file can reach main:                ║
# ║    A. CI whole-tree scan   (ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size)     ║
# ║    B. pre-commit staged scan (ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size)        ║
# ║  Method: drop two temporary 2801-line .dart files (one per directory),     ║
# ║  expect rejection, then remove them and expect the guard to pass again     ║
# ║  (negative control). The temp files never reach a commit; the index is     ║
# ║  restored exactly (only the two temp paths are ever staged/reset).         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh
# Exit 0 = guard demonstrably fires on both paths; non-zero = hole remains.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

TMP_BIN="bin/fah_size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
TMP_APP="flutter_app/lib/size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
OVER=2801   # MAX_LINES (2800) + 1

cleanup() {
  git reset -q -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

make_oversized() {
  # 2801 comment lines — syntactically valid Dart, over the ceiling.
  { echo "// size-guard probe (gh-1232 AC2 self-test) — DO NOT COMMIT"

    while [ "$i" -lt "$OVER" ]; do echo '// padding'; i=$((i + 1)); done
  } > "$1"

    echo "$out" >&2

    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejection did not name the probe file" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2

stage_size() {
  # Hook mode scopes the guard to the STAGED Dart files: the guard ratchets
  # what a commit touches, so a pre-existing oversized file elsewhere (e.g.
  # flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart, which ci.yml's guard never
  # measures — it scans lib/test/example only) cannot block an unrelated
  # commit. Non-hook runs keep the whole-tree scan below.
  if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
    local violations
    violations=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
      | grep '\.dart$' \
      | grep -vE '\.g\.dart$|\.freezed\.dart$|\.mocks\.dart$|bridge_generated|app_localizations|localizations_' \
      | while IFS= read -r f; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          lines=$(wc -l < "$f")
          if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then echo "$f: $lines lines"; fi
        done || true)
    if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
      echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
      echo "$violations" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # Same find-exec guard as ci.yml / pre-commit: no dart file over MAX_LINES.
  local dirs=""
  local d
  for d in lib test example bin; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && dirs="$dirs $d"
  done
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && [ -d flutter_app/lib ]; then
    dirs="$dirs flutter_app/lib"
  fi
  local violations
  violations=$(find $dirs -name '*.dart' \
    ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
    ! -name '*bridge_generated*.dart' ! -name '*app_localizations*.dart' \
    ! -name '*localizations_*.dart' \
    -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt '"$MAX_LINES"' ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
  if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
    echo "$violations" >&2
    exit 1

# gh-1232: [REFACTOR] CLI/app god-files at/over the 2800-line ceiling are the merge-conflict magnets — split bin/fah.dart, agent_cli.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_service.dart

## Description

**Data over the last 40 merged PRs** (2026-10-03/04, 369 file-touches): the highest-churn files are simultaneously the biggest files — classic god-file conflict physics:

| file | PRs touching it | current lines | vs 2800 guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart | **11 (27.5%)** | 2737 | 63 under |
| bin/fah.dart | 6 | **2826** | **OVER** |
| .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml | 6 | — | — |
| lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart (barrel) | 5 | 260 | — |
| lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart + agent_cli_config.dart | 5+5 | 1541/783 | — |
| lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart | 4 | **2799** | **1 under** |
| flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart | 4 | **2815** | **OVER** |

Every fourth PR fights over agent_cli.dart; every long-lived PR (30–65h lead: #1143 65h, #1163 55h, #1165 55h, #1161/#1166/#1173 49h) must rebase across the serial main queue through these same files. Size and churn compound: the bigger the file, the higher the probability two PRs edit adjacent regions.

**Also suspicious**: bin/fah.dart (2826) and agent_service.dart (2815) are OVER the pre-commit 2800-line guard yet keep landing — verify the guard actually covers them (exempt-list hole?).

**Proposed cuts:**
1. **bin/fah.dart → bin/thin + lib/src/cli/fah_commands/**: one file per subcommand family (trajectory/session/bench/…), main keeps arg routing only.
2. **agent_cli.dart**: it is already a part-of library (approval_commands etc.) — finish the pattern: slash-command tables self-register from part files so the main file stops being the edit magnet for every new command.
3. **agent_service.dart** split by concern: session lifecycle / provider wiring / secrets / mail fabric.
4. **builtin_tools.dart**: per-tool-family assembly files under lib/src/tools/.
5. **Barrel policy** (flutter_agent_harness.dart, 5/40 touches): grouped append-only export sections with a one-line convention comment, or per-subsystem mini-barrels — pick one, write it in AGENTS.md.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: bin/fah.dart, agent_service.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_cli.dart each < 2000 lines after the split; zero behavior change (existing test suites green, no public API moves without deprecation).
- AC2: the pre-commit size guard demonstrably fires on a file > 2800 in bin/ and flutter_app/ (test: temporary oversized file → hook rejects).
- AC3: re-measure after the next 40 merged PRs: agent_cli.dart touch rate < 15%, no file above 2400 lines in the top-10 churn list.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved

  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).

blocks.text:
The agent_service token diff is noisy because my crude tokenizer mangles string interpolations with nested quotes (`'$x y'` adjacent text becomes tokens like `$countmessage`) — those are all inside strings and reformatting strings across lines changes token splits. The `;` → `:` changes (8 semicolons became colons) — that's interesting. Could be from named parameters reflow? Let me look at what that is. Also `AgentNetworkControllergetagentNetwork` removed.

This crude tokenizer is unreliable for string-heavy files. Better approach: reconstruct. Since these are part/mixin files, do a smarter comparison: use `dart format` on both sides and compare line multisets after formatting? That normalizes formatting. Actually the simplest robust check: run the compiler/analyzer and tests. The PR claims tests pass. The token check for the three pure-part families (fah, agent_cli, builtin_tools, wasm_shell) is clean apart from trivial punctuation.

For agent_service, the mixin conversion is structural — extensions vs mixins changes code (`on AgentService`, `mixin` keywords). Multiset tokens should still match modulo string-mangling. The `;`→`:` delta of exactly 8 each way is worth a look. Let me find it: it could be from string interpolation mangling again (e.g. `${x};` inside a string vs outside?). Given my STR regex replaces whole strings, interpolation inside strings is hidden. But adjacent text outside strings... `;` → `:` conversion can't happen from formatting.

Let me find semicolons in main's agent_service that became colons in the new files. Approach: the multiset diff means 8 `;` tokens disappeared and 8 `:` tokens appeared. Could be ternary reformat? No — token type change means actual code edit. Maybe map literals `{'a'; ...}`? Unlikely. Could be in a doc-comment? Comments are stripped. Hmm, could be inside a string my regex mishandled: e.g. a string containing a quote: `'it\'s'`. My regex `\x27(?:[^\x27\\]|\\.)*\x27` handles escaped quotes. Triple-quoted strings `'''...'''` — regex matches first two quotes as empty string then contents leak as tokens! And multi-line strings containing `;` or `:` would leak. That's likely the explanation: a prompt/heredoc string in agent_service was reformatted (moved, line-wrapped), and its leaked content tokens shift.

Rather than perfect this, the pragmatic verification: the earlier LINE multiset diff showed lots of added string fragments — consistent with strings being split across lines differently. The compiler + full test suite are the real safety net. Let me:

4. Review ci.yml and size_guard_selftest.sh content fully.

Is it semantically relevant? The map type is `Future<void> Function(String)`. If `_applyThemeChoice` returns `Future<void>`:
- `(key) => _applyThemeChoice(...)` — arrow returns the Future directly: type `Future<void>`. OK.
- `(key) async => ...` — async arrow wraps: returns `Future<void>` (flattened). Also OK.

Both produce `Future<void> Function(String)`. Behavior: `async =>` adds one microtask delay before the body executes... actually no: `async => expr` evaluates expr eagerly when called and the future completes with its value — no extra microtask delay for the evaluation itself; the body starts synchronously. The difference: error handling — if `_applyThemeChoice` returns a Future that completes with error, `(key) =>` propagates that same future; `async =>` awaits it and re-throws on the async future — same observable behavior for callers awaiting the result. Also zone context: `async` runs the body in a new microtask context? The invocation of `_applyThemeChoice` happens synchronously within the async body... Actually in `async => e`, `e` is evaluated synchronously at call time and the result future is awaited. Observable differences are negligible (identical futures API-wise).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1232 AC2 — size-guard self-test                                        ║
# ║  Proves the 2800-line guard fires on oversized files in bin/ and           ║
# ║  flutter_app/lib/ through BOTH paths a file can reach main:                ║
# ║    A. CI whole-tree scan   (ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size)     ║
# ║    B. pre-commit staged scan (ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size)        ║
# ║  Method: drop two temporary 2801-line .dart files (one per directory),     ║
# ║  expect rejection, then remove them and expect the guard to pass again     ║
# ║  (negative control). The temp files never reach a commit; the index is     ║
# ║  restored exactly (only the two temp paths are ever staged/reset).         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh
# Exit 0 = guard demonstrably fires on both paths; non-zero = hole remains.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

TMP_BIN="bin/fah_size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
TMP_APP="flutter_app/lib/size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
OVER=2801   # MAX_LINES (2800) + 1

cleanup() {
  git reset -q -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

make_oversized() {
  # 2801 comment lines — syntactically valid Dart, over the ceiling.
  { echo "// size-guard probe (gh-1232 AC2 self-test) — DO NOT COMMIT"
    i=1
    while [ "$i" -lt "$OVER" ]; do echo '// padding'; i=$((i + 1)); done
  } > "$1"
}

expect_reject() {
  # $1 = label, $2.. = command to run (already staged temps assumed)
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  set +e
  out=$("$@" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): guard PASSED an oversized file" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "FILE SIZE"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejected, but not by the size guard:" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejection did not name the probe file" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "✅ $label: guard rejected the oversized files"

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. - **Title**: gh-1232 [REFACTOR] CLI/app god-files at/over the 2800-line ceiling are the merge-conflict magnets — split bin/fah.dart, agent_cli.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_service.dart
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1232` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 42
- **Additions**: +7651
- **Deletions**: -7253
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:12:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T18:09:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Split the four god-files into `part`-based libraries (pure mechanical moves, zero behavior change) and closed the 2800-line guard hole that let two files sail past the ceiling:

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/fah.dart` | 2889 | 224 (+6 `bin/fah_*.dart` parts) |
| `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` | 2785 | 1954 (+4 `agent_cli_{lifecycle,input,pickers,run}.dart`) |
| `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart` | 2797 | 178 (+8 `builtin_tools_<family>.dart` parts) |
| `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart` | 2896 | 1994 (+7 `agent_service_*` extension parts) |
| `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/wasm_shell.dart` | 2835 | 2728 (+1 part — pre-existing offender the new app guard exposed) |

### Key decisions
- **Parts, not packages**: every split uses the repo's established `part of` pattern so private identifiers and public signatures stay put — no API moves, no import churn. `bin/` command code stays in `bin/` (`dart:io` may not enter pure-Dart `lib/`).
- **Guard hole (AC2)**: ci.yml's size guard scanned only `lib test example`; it now scans `bin` too, and a new `flutter_app/lib` size step runs in the Flutter app analyze job. `scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh` (new) proves rejection of oversized files in both dirs through both the CI scan and the pre-commit staged scan — ran: PASSED.
- **Barrel policy (cut #5)**: grouped append-only export sections with `// ── <subsystem> ──` headers, written into AGENTS.md alongside the ceiling/split-by-parts convention.
- Slash-command self-registration skipped: command tables already live in part files; the primary held none (noted in agent-cli split report).

### How to verify
```bash
bash scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh          # AC2: guard fires on bin/ + flutter_app/
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size
dart test --concurrency=3 --exclude-tags integration   # 8863 passed, 0 failed
(cd flutter_app && flutter test test/agent_service test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart)
```
AC3 (touch-rate re-measure) is a metric for the next 40 PRs, not actionable in this change.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable

  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via

  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1232 AC2 — size-guard self-test                                        ║
# ║  Proves the 2800-line guard fires on oversized files in bin/ and           ║
# ║  flutter_app/lib/ through BOTH paths a file can reach main:                ║
# ║    A. CI whole-tree scan   (ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size)     ║
# ║    B. pre-commit staged scan (ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size)        ║
# ║  Method: drop two temporary 2801-line .dart files (one per directory),     ║
# ║  expect rejection, then remove them and expect the guard to pass again     ║
# ║  (negative control). The temp files never reach a commit; the index is     ║
# ║  restored exactly (only the two temp paths are ever staged/reset).         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh
# Exit 0 = guard demonstrably fires on both paths; non-zero = hole remains.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

TMP_BIN="bin/fah_size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
TMP_APP="flutter_app/lib/size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
OVER=2801   # MAX_LINES (2800) + 1

cleanup() {
  git reset -q -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

make_oversized() {
  # 2801 comment lines — syntactically valid Dart, over the ceiling.
  { echo "// size-guard probe (gh-1232 AC2 self-test) — DO NOT COMMIT"
    i=1
    while [ "$i" -lt "$OVER" ]; do echo '// padding'; i=$((i + 1)); done
  } > "$1"
}

expect_reject() {
  # $1 = label, $2.. = command to run (already staged temps assumed)
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  set +e
  out=$("$@" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): guard PASSED an oversized file" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "FILE SIZE"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejected, but not by the size guard:" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejection did not name the probe file" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "✅ $label: guard rejected the oversized files"
}

echo "── gh-1232 AC2 size-guard self-test ──"

# Pre-flight: the negative control must pass with NO probe files staged.
out=$(bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size 2>&1) \
  || { echo "❌ pre-flight: hook size stage fails on a clean tree:" >&2; echo "$out" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "✅ pre-flight: hook size stage passes without probes"

make_oversized "$TMP_BIN"
make_oversized "$TMP_APP"

echo "── A. CI whole-tree scan ──"
expect_reject "CI scan (bin/ + flutter_app/lib/)" \
  bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size

echo "── B. pre-commit staged scan ──"
git add -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
expect_reject "hook staged scan (bin/ + flutter_app/lib/)" \
  bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size

echo "── negative control: probes removed, guard passes again ──"
cleanup

out=$(bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size 2>&1) \
  || { echo "❌ negative control: guard still fails after probe cleanup:" >&2; echo "$out" >&2; exit 1; }
[ ! -e "$TMP_BIN" ] && [ ! -e "$TMP_APP" ] \

echo "✅ negative control: guard passes, probes gone"

echo ""
echo "╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
echo "║  ✅ AC2 SELF-TEST PASSED — the 2800-line guard fires on bin/ and           ║"
echo "║     flutter_app/ through both the CI scan and the pre-commit staged scan   ║"
echo "╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"

# gh-1232: [REFACTOR] CLI/app god-files at/over the 2800-line ceiling are the merge-conflict magnets — split bin/fah.dart, agent_cli.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_service.dart

## Description

**Data over the last 40 merged PRs** (2026-10-03/04, 369 file-touches): the highest-churn files are simultaneously the biggest files — classic god-file conflict physics:

| file | PRs touching it | current lines | vs 2800 guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart | **11 (27.5%)** | 2737 | 63 under |
| bin/fah.dart | 6 | **2826** | **OVER** |
| .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml | 6 | — | — |
| lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart (barrel) | 5 | 260 | — |
| lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart + agent_cli_config.dart | 5+5 | 1541/783 | — |
| lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart | 4 | **2799** | **1 under** |
| flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart | 4 | **2815** | **OVER** |

Every fourth PR fights over agent_cli.dart; every long-lived PR (30–65h lead: #1143 65h, #1163 55h, #1165 55h, #1161/#1166/#1173 49h) must rebase across the serial main queue through these same files. Size and churn compound: the bigger the file, the higher the probability two PRs edit adjacent regions.

**Also suspicious**: bin/fah.dart (2826) and agent_service.dart (2815) are OVER the pre-commit 2800-line guard yet keep landing — verify the guard actually covers them (exempt-list hole?).

**Proposed cuts:**
1. **bin/fah.dart → bin/thin + lib/src/cli/fah_commands/**: one file per subcommand family (trajectory/session/bench/…), main keeps arg routing only.
2. **agent_cli.dart**: it is already a part-of library (approval_commands etc.) — finish the pattern: slash-command tables self-register from part files so the main file stops being the edit magnet for every new command.
3. **agent_service.dart** split by concern: session lifecycle / provider wiring / secrets / mail fabric.
4. **builtin_tools.dart**: per-tool-family assembly files under lib/src/tools/.
5. **Barrel policy** (flutter_agent_harness.dart, 5/40 touches): grouped append-only export sections with a one-line convention comment, or per-subsystem mini-barrels — pick one, write it in AGENTS.md.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: bin/fah.dart, agent_service.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_cli.dart each < 2000 lines after the split; zero behavior change (existing test suites green, no public API moves without deprecation).
- AC2: the pre-commit size guard demonstrably fires on a file > 2800 in bin/ and flutter_app/ (test: temporary oversized file → hook rejects).
- AC3: re-measure after the next 40 merged PRs: agent_cli.dart touch rate < 15%, no file above 2400 lines in the top-10 churn list.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1232 AC2 — size-guard self-test                                        ║
# ║  Proves the 2800-line guard fires on oversized files in bin/ and           ║
# ║  flutter_app/lib/ through BOTH paths a file can reach main:                ║
# ║    A. CI whole-tree scan   (ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size)     ║
# ║    B. pre-commit staged scan (ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size)        ║
# ║  Method: drop two temporary 2801-line .dart files (one per directory),     ║
# ║  expect rejection, then remove them and expect the guard to pass again     ║
# ║  (negative control). The temp files never reach a commit; the index is     ║
# ║  restored exactly (only the two temp paths are ever staged/reset).         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh
# Exit 0 = guard demonstrably fires on both paths; non-zero = hole remains.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

TMP_BIN="bin/fah_size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
TMP_APP="flutter_app/lib/size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
OVER=2801   # MAX_LINES (2800) + 1

cleanup() {
  git reset -q -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

make_oversized() {
  # 2801 comment lines — syntactically valid Dart, over the ceiling.
  { echo "// size-guard probe (gh-1232 AC2 self-test) — DO NOT COMMIT"
    i=1
    while [ "$i" -lt "$OVER" ]; do echo '// padding'; i=$((i + 1)); done
  } > "$1"
}

expect_reject() {
  # $1 = label, $2.. = command to run (already staged temps assumed)
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  set +e
  out=$("$@" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): guard PASSED an oversized file" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "FILE SIZE"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejected, but not by the size guard:" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejection did not name the probe file" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "✅ $label: guard rejected the oversized files"
}

echo "── gh-1232 AC2 size-guard self-test ──"

# Pre-flight: the negative control must pass with NO probe files staged.
out=$(bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size 2>&1) \
  || { echo "❌ pre-flight: hook size stage fails on a clean tree:" >&2; echo "$out" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "✅ pre-flight: hook size stage passes without probes"

make_oversized "$TMP_BIN"
make_oversized "$TMP_APP"

echo "── A. CI whole-tree scan ──"
expect_reject "CI scan (bin/ + flutter_app/lib/)" \
  bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size

echo "── B. pre-commit staged scan ──"
git add -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
expect_reject "hook staged scan (bin/ + flutter_app/lib/)" \
  bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size

echo "── negative control: probes removed, guard passes again ──"
cleanup
trap - EXIT
out=$(bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size 2>&1) \
  || { echo "❌ negative control: guard still fails after probe cleanup:" >&2; echo "$out" >&2; exit 1; }
[ ! -e "$TMP_BIN" ] && [ ! -e "$TMP_APP" ] \
  || { echo "❌ probe files left behind" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "✅ negative control: guard passes, probes gone"

echo ""
echo "╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
echo "║  ✅ AC2 SELF-TEST PASSED — the 2800-line guard fires on bin/ and           ║"
echo "║     flutter_app/ through both the CI scan and the pre-commit staged scan   ║"
echo "╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"

# gh-1232: [REFACTOR] CLI/app god-files at/over the 2800-line ceiling are the merge-conflict magnets — split bin/fah.dart, agent_cli.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_service.dart

## Description

**Data over the last 40 merged PRs** (2026-10-03/04, 369 file-touches): the highest-churn files are simultaneously the biggest files — classic god-file conflict physics:

| file | PRs touching it | current lines | vs 2800 guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart | **11 (27.5%)** | 2737 | 63 under |
| bin/fah.dart | 6 | **2826** | **OVER** |
| .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml | 6 | — | — |
| lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart (barrel) | 5 | 260 | — |
| lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart + agent_cli_config.dart | 5+5 | 1541/783 | — |
| lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart | 4 | **2799** | **1 under** |
| flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart | 4 | **2815** | **OVER** |

Every fourth PR fights over agent_cli.dart; every long-lived PR (30–65h lead: #1143 65h, #1163 55h, #1165 55h, #1161/#1166/#1173 49h) must rebase across the serial main queue through these same files. Size and churn compound: the bigger the file, the higher the probability two PRs edit adjacent regions.

**Also suspicious**: bin/fah.dart (2826) and agent_service.dart (2815) are OVER the pre-commit 2800-line guard yet keep landing — verify the guard actually covers them (exempt-list hole?).

**Proposed cuts:**
1. **bin/fah.dart → bin/thin + lib/src/cli/fah_commands/**: one file per subcommand family (trajectory/session/bench/…), main keeps arg routing only.
2. **agent_cli.dart**: it is already a part-of library (approval_commands etc.) — finish the pattern: slash-command tables self-register from part files so the main file stops being the edit magnet for every new command.
3. **agent_service.dart** split by concern: session lifecycle / provider wiring / secrets / mail fabric.
4. **builtin_tools.dart**: per-tool-family assembly files under lib/src/tools/.
5. **Barrel policy** (flutter_agent_harness.dart, 5/40 touches): grouped append-only export sections with a one-line convention comment, or per-subsystem mini-barrels — pick one, write it in AGENTS.md.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: bin/fah.dart, agent_service.dart, builtin_tools.dart, agent_cli.dart each < 2000 lines after the split; zero behavior change (existing test suites green, no public API moves without deprecation).
- AC2: the pre-commit size guard demonstrably fires on a file > 2800 in bin/ and flutter_app/ (test: temporary oversized file → hook rejects).
- AC3: re-measure after the next 40 merged PRs: agent_cli.dart touch rate < 15%, no file above 2400 lines in the top-10 churn list.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved

  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).

messages.preview: The agent_service token diff is polluted by my tokenizer mangling multi-line strings. A cleaner check: `dart format` both sides canonically, then compare line multisets.

blocks.text:
The agent_service token diff is noisy because my crude tokenizer mangles string interpolations with nested quotes (`'$x y'` adjacent text becomes tokens like `$countmessage`) — those are all inside strings and reformatting strings across lines changes token splits. The `;` → `:` changes (8 semicolons became colons) — that's interesting. Could be from named parameters reflow? Let me look at what that is. Also `AgentNetworkControllergetagentNetwork` removed.

This crude tokenizer is unreliable for string-heavy files. Better approach: reconstruct. Since these are part/mixin files, do a smarter comparison: use `dart format` on both sides and compare line multisets after formatting? That normalizes formatting. Actually the simplest robust check: run the compiler/analyzer and tests. The PR claims tests pass. The token check for the three pure-part families (fah, agent_cli, builtin_tools, wasm_shell) is clean apart from trivial punctuation.

For agent_service, the mixin conversion is structural — extensions vs mixins changes code (`on AgentService`, `mixin` keywords). Multiset tokens should still match modulo string-mangling. The `;`→`:` delta of exactly 8 each way is worth a look. Let me find it: it could be from string interpolation mangling again (e.g. `${x};` inside a string vs outside?). Given my STR regex replaces whole strings, interpolation inside strings is hidden. But adjacent text outside strings... `;` → `:` conversion can't happen from formatting.

Let me find semicolons in main's agent_service that became colons in the new files. Approach: the multiset diff means 8 `;` tokens disappeared and 8 `:` tokens appeared. Could be ternary reformat? No — token type change means actual code edit. Maybe map literals `{'a'; ...}`? Unlikely. Could be in a doc-comment? Comments are stripped. Hmm, could be inside a string my regex mishandled: e.g. a string containing a quote: `'it\'s'`. My regex `\x27(?:[^\x27\\]|\\.)*\x27` handles escaped quotes. Triple-quoted strings `'''...'''` — regex matches first two quotes as empty string then contents leak as tokens! And multi-line strings containing `;` or `:` would leak. That's likely the explanation: a prompt/heredoc string in agent_service was reformatted (moved, line-wrapped), and its leaked content tokens shift.

Rather than perfect this, the pragmatic verification: the earlier LINE multiset diff showed lots of added string fragments — consistent with strings being split across lines differently. The compiler + full test suite are the real safety net. Let me:

1. Check the `;`→`:` concretely by searching for a pattern.
2. Run dart analyze.
3. Run the wiring tests + a subset.
4. Review ci.yml and size_guard_selftest.sh content fully.
5. Check AGENTS.md claims match ci_fast_gate.sh behavior (guard coverage claim).

Is it semantically relevant? The map type is `Future<void> Function(String)`. If `_applyThemeChoice` returns `Future<void>`:
- `(key) => _applyThemeChoice(...)` — arrow returns the Future directly: type `Future<void>`. OK.
- `(key) async => ...` — async arrow wraps: returns `Future<void>` (flattened). Also OK.

Both produce `Future<void> Function(String)`. Behavior: `async =>` adds one microtask delay before the body executes... actually no: `async => expr` evaluates expr eagerly when called and the future completes with its value — no extra microtask delay for the evaluation itself; the body starts synchronously. The difference: error handling — if `_applyThemeChoice` returns a Future that completes with error, `(key) =>` propagates that same future; `async =>` awaits it and re-throws on the async future — same observable behavior for callers awaiting the result. Also zone context: `async` runs the body in a new microtask context? The invocation of `_applyThemeChoice` happens synchronously within the async body... Actually in `async => e`, `e` is evaluated synchronously at call time and the result future is awaited. Observable differences are negligible (identical futures API-wise).

BUT: why was it added? Maybe because `_applyThemeChoice` was moved to a part file where its inferred return differs? Or the analyzer flagged something. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1232 AC2 — size-guard self-test                                        ║
# ║  Proves the 2800-line guard fires on oversized files in bin/ and           ║
# ║  flutter_app/lib/ through BOTH paths a file can reach main:                ║
# ║    A. CI whole-tree scan   (ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size)     ║
# ║    B. pre-commit staged scan (ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size)        ║
# ║  Method: drop two temporary 2801-line .dart files (one per directory),     ║
# ║  expect rejection, then remove them and expect the guard to pass again     ║
# ║  (negative control). The temp files never reach a commit; the index is     ║
# ║  restored exactly (only the two temp paths are ever staged/reset).         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/size_guard_selftest.sh
# Exit 0 = guard demonstrably fires on both paths; non-zero = hole remains.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

TMP_BIN="bin/fah_size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
TMP_APP="flutter_app/lib/size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"
OVER=2801   # MAX_LINES (2800) + 1

cleanup() {
  git reset -q -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

make_oversized() {
  # 2801 comment lines — syntactically valid Dart, over the ceiling.
  { echo "// size-guard probe (gh-1232 AC2 self-test) — DO NOT COMMIT"
    i=1
    while [ "$i" -lt "$OVER" ]; do echo '// padding'; i=$((i + 1)); done
  } > "$1"
}

expect_reject() {
  # $1 = label, $2.. = command to run (already staged temps assumed)
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  set +e
  out=$("$@" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): guard PASSED an oversized file" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "FILE SIZE"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejected, but not by the size guard:" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -q "size_guard_probe_tmp.dart"; then
    echo "❌ AC2 SELF-TEST FAILED ($label): rejection did not name the probe file" >&2
    echo "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "✅ $label: guard rejected the oversized files"
}

echo "── gh-1232 AC2 size-guard self-test ──"

# Pre-flight: the negative control must pass with NO probe files staged.
out=$(bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook --stages size 2>&1) \
  || { echo "❌ pre-flight: hook size stage fails on a clean tree:" >&2; echo "$out" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "✅ pre-flight: hook size stage passes without probes"

make_oversized "$TMP_BIN"
make_oversized "$TMP_APP"

echo "── A. CI whole-tree scan ──"
expect_reject "CI scan (bin/ + flutter_app/lib/)" \
  bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --scope all --stages size

echo "── B. pre-commit staged scan ──"
git add -- "$TMP_BIN" "$TMP_APP"
expect_reject "hook staged scan (bin/ + flutter_app/lib/)" \

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
